title: How to tell whether an Amazon deal is worth it
description: Check the exact product, reference price and delivered cost before buying. Use DealScout’s calculator to compare two offers by price per unit.
intro: A large discount can be worth a closer look, but the percentage alone does not tell you whether an offer fits your needs. Start with the product you want, check what is included, then compare the amount you will actually pay. This guide gives you a repeatable checklist and a calculator for comparing two equivalent offers.
disclosure: This guide follows DealScout’s pricing policy and the linked Amazon reference-price guidance. It does not represent hands-on product testing.

sections.title: 1. Match the exact product
paragraphs: Compare the model number, generation, size, color, condition and included accessories. A cheaper listing for a different version is a different offer. For multipacks, check the number of items and the amount in each item before comparing prices.
Ask whether you would buy this exact product without the discount label. An attractive price does not make an unsuitable size, incompatible device or unnecessary extra quantity useful.

sections.title: 2. Understand the discount’s baseline
paragraphs: DealScout’s percentage savings compare the checked offer price with the reference price supplied by the listing. Amazon uses different reference-price labels, and the reference shown can change. Read the label attached to the crossed-out price rather than assuming it describes the lowest price you could have paid before.

For example, an offer at $60 compared with a $100 reference price shows 40% savings against that reference. This calculation alone does not establish a historical low or prove that another seller’s current price is higher. DealScout does not claim those comparisons without supporting data.

sections.title: 3. Compare the delivered cost
paragraphs: Use the checkout figures for your address: item price, shipping, tax and any discount you are eligible to apply. Include membership or subscription conditions in your decision. An offer that depends on a subscription is not equivalent to a one-time purchase unless those terms work for you.

The calculator below uses amounts you enter; it does not retrieve checkout prices, estimate tax or apply coupons. Enter tax after any applicable discount as shown at checkout. If a charge is unknown, the comparison is provisional. For multipacks, use the same quantity unit on both sides—items with items, ounces with ounces or milliliters with milliliters.

sections.title: A smaller checkout total can have the same unit cost
paragraphs: Illustrative example: Offer A costs $18 for six items, plus $3 shipping. With no tax or discount entered, its delivered total is $21, or $3.50 per item. Offer B costs $16 for four equivalent items, with free shipping and an eligible $2 discount. Its delivered total is $14, also $3.50 per item.

Neither offer is cheaper per item in this example. Offer B requires less money at checkout; Offer A supplies more items. Choose the quantity you expect to use and compare the purchase terms. These numbers are a worked example, not live Amazon offers.

sections.title: 4. Check the seller and purchase terms
paragraphs: Review who sells and ships the selected offer, the delivery estimate, product condition, return terms and any warranty information that matters to you. Confirm these details for the selected variant. A product title or star rating does not settle every question about the particular offer.

For products with ongoing costs, consider the supplies or accessories you will need. A coffee maker’s machine price is only part of the cost if you also need capsules, filters or cleaning supplies. Use manufacturer specifications to resolve compatibility questions before ordering.

sections.title: 5. Recheck the offer before buying
paragraphs: DealScout public listings require a price check within the past 24 hours, but a price or available variant can change between checks. Open the product’s deal page to see its check time, then confirm the selected offer and final amount on Amazon before placing the order.

Our automated checks select offers that meet the site’s pricing and product-data rules. They do not mean that we have tested the product or that every published item is a personal editor recommendation. Read any separate DealScout Pick note for the editor’s stated rationale.
